author: Orange Wang
description:
US President Donald Trump is likely to continue on a path of trying to stabilise ties with Beijing – even if the Democrats flip the House of Representatives, according to analysts.
But they said if the Republicans lost control of the House in this week’s midterm elections, the framework of “strategic stability” agreed to by Washington and Beijing could be put to the test.
One Chinese academic warned that other Republicans could pose the biggest risk to Sino-American ties in Trump’s final two...
title: Will ‘strategic stability’ with China go out the window if Trump loses the midterms?

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
US President Donald Trump ended the midterm campaign season on Monday by calling the Democratic Party’s candidates the “most extreme and dangerous” in American history, the day before voters decide which party controls Congress.
Speaking at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, which reopened after a renovation by his administration, Trump called the elections “the most important midterm, I believe, in our lifetime”.
“These are the most dangerous candidates ever put up,” he...
title: Trump closes midterm campaign calling Democratic candidates ‘most dangerous ever’

author: Zhang Tong
description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is now solving maths puzzles that have long stumped humans, prompting mathematicians around the world, including in China, to ponder not only whether machines will replace them, but also what achievement and research in their field will mean in the future.
In early October, OpenAI released manuscripts showing progress on 372 categories of mathematical problems, including many which have long defied solutions. This week, the American AI firm announced three further...
title: As AI solves maths puzzles faster than humans, mathematicians face uncertain future

author: William Zheng
description:
Retired cadres were consulted during the eight-month drafting of a landmark document on building China’s Communist Party endorsed at a major political meeting in Beijing last week, according to state media.
A detailed account published by Xinhua on Monday gave a behind-the-scenes look into how the 20th Central Committee finalised its resolution on “persevering with full and rigorous party self-governance”, adopted at the fifth plenum, which ended on Thursday.
The 17,000-Chinese character,...
title: How Xi Jinping and Communist Party elders shaped key plenum document addressing wrongdoing

author: Eve Qiao
description:
Three ancient wooden boats unearthed in Beijing and dating back about 1,800 years offer new evidence of shipbuilding technology and cultural exchanges between ancient China and the rest of the world, according to researchers.
The researchers unveiled details of “the first physical evidence of ancient inland water transport” in the Chinese capital at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Beijing Public Archaeology Season on Saturday, according to an official social media account of the Beijing...
title: Echoes of Rome in ancient China? What Beijing’s 1,800-year-old ship find reveals

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven of the most interesting and important news stories covering US-China relations from the past few weeks. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. The ‘Queen of the Chinese’ and a forgotten history on the US-Mexico border

Interest in the history of the Chinese community in the Lone Star State is growing. “There’s a real resurrection in understanding the influence of the Chinese in Texas,” Linda Chew, a retired judge in the US state’s...
title: ‘Queen of the Chinese’, drone war fears, cancer drug on sale: 7 US-China relations reads

author: Amber Wang
description:
Pakistan’s contract to buy Chinese Z-10ME attack helicopters covers 30 airframes, according to an image circulating on Chinese social media.
The image was shared by a prominent military blogger on Sunday and marks the first time a concrete number for Pakistan’s fleet of the helicopters has surfaced since Islamabad officially inducted them into service in August last year.
In the post, the blogger known as Sashoujian said that on July 11 China National Aero-Technology Import and Export...
title: Blogger may have revealed how many Z-10ME helicopters Pakistan bought from China

author: William Zheng
description:
China’s ruling Communist Party has overhauled its personnel process in its search for clean and battle-tested cadres ahead of next year’s major leadership reshuffle.
New rules were included in a resolution adopted at the 20th Central Committee’s fifth plenum last Thursday and published by state news agency Xinhua on Sunday.
Analysts said that as provincial and ministerial reshuffles begin ahead of the 21st party congress, the fifth plenum sent a clear message: Beijing wants proven crisis...
title: China’s fifth plenum: cadre promotion rules overhauled, focusing on problem-solving

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan is tightening its military service exemption rules in a sweeping overhaul expected to halve the exemption rate and add thousands of conscripts to the armed forces each year as the island grapples with persistent manpower shortages.
Under the revised standards, which took effect last week, men will generally be exempt on weight grounds only if their body mass index (BMI) exceeds 45, while the height threshold for exemption has been lowered to 144cm (4.7 feet).
Rules covering hypertension...
title: Raising the bar: Taiwan trims draft exemptions to add thousands to armed forces

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
China’s top diplomat has again stressed the need for a political settlement to strife in the Middle East, telling a senior Iranian official in Beijing on Monday that armed conflict was not the way out.
“As conflicts in the Middle East drag on and risk further spillover, dialogue and negotiation remain the only viable path forward,” Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council.
“All parties should … focus on a political settlement in a rational and...
title: Talks are the only way out, China tells Iran as US threat hangs over Middle East

author: Ling Xin
description:
Turkey has signed America’s rule book for the moon, but its first ride to the lunar south pole – the icy region both Washington and Beijing are racing to reach – will probably come from China.
A team of more than 120 students and professors at Middle East Technical University (METU) in Ankara has built prototypes of two AI-powered rovers for Chang’e-8, a Chinese mission originally planned for 2028.
Turkey is not part of the International Lunar Research Station, a base China plans to build on the...
title: Turkey signed US-led Artemis Accords. Its moon rovers will hitch a ride with China

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Beijing is accelerating production of its Type 071 amphibious transport docks by expanding construction to a second shipyard, potentially strengthening its ability to move troops and military equipment across the Taiwan Strait in a conflict.
The expansion comes amid long-standing United States assessments that Beijing lacks enough landing ships and logistical support for a large-scale assault on Taiwan, suggesting the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) may be moving to address a significant...
title: Beijing doubles down on Type 071 amphibious warships, signalling a Taiwan focus

author: Fan Chen,Carol Yang
description:
China and Oman have called for a peaceful resolution and full ceasefire between the US and Iran, stressing that safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz must be restored.
The call came during talks in Beijing on Monday between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq.
In their joint statement, Beijing and Muscat encouraged the United States and Iran to resume dialogue and reach a “comprehensive agreement that includes the nuclear issue”.
The two sides also affirmed that...
title: China and Oman unite in Mideast peace call on sultan’s ‘historic’ Beijing visit

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage of China’s fifth plenum. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. ‘Unwritten rules’ become newest target in Communist Party’s war on corruption
The Communist Party of China has pledged to vigorously crack down on the “unwritten rules” that enable corruption in the party, deepening its long-running campaign to keep officials in line.
2. At China’s fifth plenum, Communist Party puts discipline and loyalty to Xi...
title: China’s fifth plenum: everything you need to know from the war on corruption to promotions

author: Chao Kong
description:
Some high-pressure turbine blades in US-made GE Aerospace engines powering Boeing 787 aircraft have suffered unexpectedly early damage, leaving airlines with a difficult choice: replace the engines or continue flying under strict inspection requirements, according to a Chinese aviation specialist.
The findings raise questions about the reliability of American aerospace products amid growing scrutiny of US manufacturing quality. According to the study, cracks can develop in some blades within...
title: Chinese mechanic reports short-lived GE engine blades in Boeing 787

description: This article is the official English translation of the original Chinese document released by Xinhua.
title: China’s fifth plenum readout

author: Holly Chik
description:
Chinese researchers have mapped how energy from surface wind surges thousands of metres into the seabed, revealing massive underwater conduits they called “inertial chimneys”.
The discovery, based on data collected by a US-funded ocean sensor array off the east coast of Japan, coupled with future long-term underwater monitoring, can provide underwater acoustic environmental support for marine detection and communication, the team said.
The scientists from the Institute of Oceanology of the...
title: Chinese scientists found giant ‘chimneys’ in deep water that could alter submarine warfare

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
Joshua Cooper Ramo is chairman and CEO of Sornay, an investment and advisory firm. Previously he was CEO of Kissinger Associates. Ramo is the author of the new book Darwin’s Lock: America, China and the Shared Future of Nations. His 2004 analysis of “the Beijing consensus” contrasted the Western and Chinese economic development models. He is the author of two New York Times bestselling books and now lives in Shanghai with his family.
For other interviews in the Open Questions series, click...
title: Ex-Kissinger partner on how China, US can evolve together or die together

author: Phoebe Zhang,William Zheng
description:
Construction workers have been working late into the night in downtown Shenzhen as the city makes its final preparations for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in two weeks’ time.
On a weekday night, a South China Morning Post reporter saw at least 50 construction workers gathered at an intersection about 1km (just over half a mile) from the Apec venues in the central district of Futian, laying down pebbles and planting trees along the pavements.
The main road that leads up to the...
title: Apec China summit: from traffic curbs to tree planting, Shenzhen’s plans enter final phase

author: Mark Magnier
description:
Tuesday’s US midterm election is both hugely consequential and not so consequential even as the world waits to see the American voters’ verdict on Donald Trump’s presidency – and the impact that verdict will have on his temperament, plans and possible petulant response, analysts and former government officials said.
On the one hand, an expected strong showing by opposition Democrats could bring more Congressional scrutiny over some of the most unconventional, maximalist and disruptive policies...
title: Will losing US midterms see Trump double down or signal beginning of the end?
